title: Vector
notes: A vector has magnitude and direction. Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors; distance, speed, mass and energy are scalars.
Choose axes and resolve A into Ax=A cosθ, Ay=A sinθ when θ is measured from +x. Components are signed according to their direction and are added separately.
Worked example: a 10 N force at 30° above +x has Fx=8.66 N and Fy=5.00 N. Recovering its magnitude gives √(8.66²+5.00²)≈10 N.
Add vectors by components: (3,4)+(−1,2)=(2,6), with magnitude √40≈6.32. The dot product ABcosθ is scalar; the cross product has magnitude ABsinθ and a perpendicular direction.
Check a result against the diagram: the resultant should lie between the component directions, and its magnitude should not exceed the sum of component magnitudes.

Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors. Distance, speed, mass and energy are scalars. Two vectors of equal magnitude can add to anything between zero and twice one of them, depending on the angle, so the magnitude alone never fixes the resultant.
confusion: The angle in component formulas must be measured from the stated axis.
A negative component indicates direction, not negative length.
A symbol is not a number until the unit is named.
A proportional relation is not an equality until the constant is included.
A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.
A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.
